subject: Aperture - Output Ownership, Training Opt-Out & Routing Playbook
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aperture.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: aperture-legal@aperture.io
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aperture - proposed redlines: output ownership + training opt-out

Ben —

Thanks for the call earlier. Our legal team attached a short redline (Aperture-Requested-Redlines.docx) with three core asks for the Order Form and MSA: 1) explicit assignment of output title for customer-generated content, 2) a training/data-use opt-out for models trained on our customer content, and 3) a narrow feedback license limited to telemetry and anonymized signals.

We flagged a couple of related operational asks as comments: audit log retention window, proof of deletion workflow, and a fallback routing policy if Redwood Dedicated cannot honor the opt-out (we proposed automatic routing to a Private deployment or an isolated model pool).

Can you confirm Redwood's position and whether you can accept the proposed wording or suggest alternative language? We are trying to keep procurement moving this week.

Best,
Liam
Legal Ops — Aperture Innovations

Attachment: Aperture-Requested-Redlines.docx (docx)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aperture.io>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aperture - proposed redlines: output ownership + training opt-out

Liam —

Thanks for sending this over and for being explicit about the scope. Appreciate the urgency — we can move quickly. Two quick notes from a commercial/sales side before I loop Legal/PM:
- Assignment of customer-generated output: we generally grant customers broad rights to their customer content and to results derived from it, but assignment language is sensitive for commercial models. I will route this to Legal + Product to propose compatible wording (e.g., "customer retains title to customer content and exclusive rights to outputs produced solely from that content").
- Training opt-out: we support an explicit opt-out for the hosted API and Dedicated pools; for Private deployments we can provide firm guarantees. We need Legal to confirm on fallback routing (we've had asks to route to a 'no-training' pool).

Looping in Jordan (policy) and Laura (legal) to propose redline-friendly language and an operational playbook we can include in the SOW/Order Form. I will keep you posted with a proposed compromise by Monday.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aperture - proposed redlines: output ownership + training opt-out

Team —

I reviewed Aperture's redlines. High-level takeaways:
1) Output ownership: we can accept customer title to outputs that are produced solely from the customer's provided prompts and content. We should avoid a blanket assignment of model-derived IP (our models and improvements remain Redwood's). Proposed clause: "Customer retains title to Customer Content and to Outputs that are solely generated from Customer Content; Redwood retains ownership of its pre-existing models and any model improvements developed independent of Customer Content."

2) Training/Data use opt-out: we can offer an opt-out scoped to their tenant/data and to models served under their dedicated pool. For hosted shared models, we will commit to not use their data for model training if they opt out, and to route requests to a no-training variant when available. We need an explicit operational SOW: what 'no-training' means, deletion timelines, telemetry retention.

3) Feedback license: propose a narrow license for telemetry and aggregated usage stats for performance monitoring. Avoid granting rights to use customer outputs for model improvement unless explicitly opted in.

I'll draft redline language for the Order Form and a short "Consent & Routing Playbook" to attach to the SOW that covers: opt-out enrollment process, routing fallback (Private deployment / isolated pool), audit evidence (deletion logs, attestation), and SLA impacts.

Marissa — please coordinate with Product/Infra for actual routing feasibility and timing. Jordan — please review the proposed clause for any operational/regulatory flag.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aperture - proposed redlines: output ownership + training opt-out

Quick product check-in:
- Routing: we can provision an isolated inference pool (Dedicated) or a Private deployment; the "no-training" label will be enforced by disabling feedback ingestion and removing any request/response data from training pipelines. Timeline: Dedicated pool provisioning ~2-3 weeks after PO; Private deployment depends on customer infra readiness (variable).
- Auditability: we can emit deletion and routing logs and provide a signed attestation monthly. We will need Aperture to specify the retention window they want.
- SLA: routing to fallback (Private) may add latency and additional costs. We'll document the latency delta and cost assumptions in the playbook.

I'll draft a short ops playbook to attach to the Order Form that outlines enrollment, routing, evidence, and escalation contacts.

Marissa Cole
Product Ops — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aperture.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aperture - proposed redlines: output ownership + training opt-out

Liam —

Attached is our first-pass compromise and an operational playbook (OrderForm_v3.pdf). Key points:
- Output title: we accept customer title for outputs generated solely from their content (language as Laura proposed).
- Training opt-out: we will not use Customer Content to train models if Aperture opts out; we will route to an isolated pool. The opt-out is applied per-account and must be requested through the onboarding SOW.
- Feedback license: we request a limited license to use anonymized telemetry for monitoring and security; no rights to retrain models on Aperture outputs without explicit opt-in.

Next steps: Please confirm acceptance of the compromise so Procurement can proceed with PO. If you need the private deployment SOW, Marissa can provide timing and cost estimates.

Thanks,
Ben

Attachment: OrderForm_v3.pdf (pdf)

If you can add those two pieces, we'll aim to sign the Order Form this week.

Thanks,
Liam
